long.text: Signups increased from 212 to 301 across the eight weeks in the requested range. The largest change followed the pricing-page launch, but this query alone cannot show whether that launch caused the increase. Team-plan signups rose more slowly than personal-plan signups. I used the same Monday boundary in both queries, excluded deleted test accounts, and kept cancellations in a separate column so the team can compare acquisition with retention.

populated.name: signups_by_week.sql
populated.code:
select date_trunc('week', created_at) as week,
       count(*) as signups
from accounts
where created_at >= now() - interval '8 weeks'
group by 1
order by 1;
populated.result: Signups grew from 212 to 301 a week, up 42%.

populated.name: cancellations_by_week.sql
populated.result: Cancellations stayed between 8 and 14 per week.

long.name: signups_and_cancellations_by_week_for_riverside_launch.sql
long.code:
with weekly_signups as (
  select date_trunc('week', created_at) as week, plan, count(*) as signups
  from accounts
  where created_at >= timestamp '2026-02-09 00:00:00'
    and deleted_at is null
  group by week, plan
)
select week, plan, signups
from weekly_signups
order by week, plan;
long.result: Across eight complete Monday-to-Sunday weeks, signups increased from 212 to 301. Team-plan signups increased from 48 to 67. The result excludes deleted test accounts and does not include cancellations; compare it with the separate cancellation-events query before treating the change as net growth.
